I doubt if this is going to be part of .NET 8 as it is too late.  The earliest, hence, would be .NET 9. And I don' think it is relevant that your org recommends LTS only, as this change will be part of `DiagnosticSource` package, which is out-of-band, and is not tired to the actual .NET runtime.

https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/telemetry-stability.md

Take notice that the schema URL support is required by OpenTelemetry specification since [2021-06-07](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/releases/tag/v1.4.0) (sic!).

I don't think so. As the instrumentation libraries are expected to move to stable in couple months from what i heard (though there are lot of pending issues)

The spec which talks about schema_url usages (transformation etc.)m fixed telemetry schema etc. are still experimental, with no sign of moving to stable. Adding some context on how SchemaURL is useful:

SchemaURL looks like this: `https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.29.0` and has two major parts:
- `opentelemetry.io` represents the authority - who owns the schema. I can easily envision `https://aka.ms/otel/azure/sdk/schemas/1.42.0` and would publish one for Azure SDK in the future. 
- `1.29.0` represents SemVer version. We should be able to evolve it and add stability suffix

The schema URL is useful even without the content behind it - it can be treated as an opaque string, or string with specific format containing authority and version. 
The content provided under this URL is evolving, it has a huge potential, but de-facto is not used today.

--------

1. As a user I want to know what schema certain library/app/component emits. It maybe OTel semconv, 
   custom schema created by my company, etc. It helps me with:
   - knowing the source of telemetry schema (otel, my company, someone else)
   - knowing the version when debugging telemetry-related issues.
   - knowing when things are updated and get notified (e.g. via an alert) so I can adjust my dashboards and queries
   
2. As a client library or a service that emits telemetry, I need a way to tell my users which telemetry schema my component follows.
   I can document it, but auto-updates happen and it could be hard to determine what version is used in runtime.
   If I publish my own conventions, I'm making it explicit to my users. 
   
   I can additionally communicate stability level of the conventions by including GA/preview in the SemVer version (`https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.29.0-dev`).
   I can document that users can rely on this field when writing queries/alerts if it indicates stable version and following SemVer compatibility.
   
3. As a telemetry backend (processor, exporter) I may need to map otel attributes from otel schema to my own. To perform such mapping,  in a general case, I need to understand if the data follows the schema I support. If it does, I can write mappings for 
   specific version and/or optimize them based on it.
   
4. As a future-proof and very advanced telemetry backend, I want to use the schema definition provided on this URL to upgrade/downgrade that telemetry to the version I work best with. This is still in flight.
   
---------
What happens without SchemaURL:

- As a user, I need to look into each of my libs docs (for current version) to learn which conventions they emit.
- If telemetry changes (e.g. new attribute pops up) it's hard for me to understand if it has changed because my app started doing something new or lib changed and now follows updated telemetry schema
- As a backend, if I want to support multiple unstable versions, I have to support all combinations of attributes/metrics in each versions. I have no means to fail fast and  drop/optimize things I don't support yet or anymore.
  
  Imagine you're writing a backend and receive a request. You probably can serve it, but you need to explore the body to guess  which API version client was following. 
  It all works reasonably well until you need to upgrade, route based on version, apply different logic, etc.

We have a lot of breaking changes in experimental semconv - there is a big need for schema transformation that depends on schema url - people are building it.

It's expected that we'll evolve areas of OTel Semconv like GenAI after they stabilize and have v2+ in years to come. Upgrade without versioning is hard or impossible. Versioning helps backends to handle it almost gracefully

---------
Schema URL is 

- [stable in OTel spec](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/0fdbbbf032f06be3092cd4714378bc1c0c40caac/specification/schemas/README.md#schema-url)
- it's specified when tracer/meter/logger [is created](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/0fdbbbf032f06be3092cd4714378bc1c0c40caac/specification/trace/api.md#get-a-tracer)
- passed over [otlp in instrumentation scope](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto/blob/main/opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1/trace.proto#L82)
- [supported](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/0fdbbbf032f06be3092cd4714378bc1c0c40caac/spec-compliance-matrix.md#traces) by Go, Java, [JS](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopen-telemetry%2Fopentelemetry-js+schemaurl&type=code), Python, C++ OTel SDKs
- we set it in Azure SDKs in [other languages](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-java/blob/139081a4a2f5918e59cac2a3ab8b109296e52508/sdk/core/azure-core-tracing-opentelemetry/src/main/java/com/azure/core/tracing/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryTracer.java#L112) and have to use [custom attribute](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/5f8dff583da260a4e3e5fe87af53ca3cdf89cfe6/sdk/core/Azure.Core/src/Shared/DiagnosticScope.cs#L287) in .NET. This is part of our [contract with AzMon](https://msazure.visualstudio.com/One/_git/CommonSchema?path=/v4.0/Mappings/AzureSDKs.md) on versioning.

review_comments: It defaults to empty but it's allowed to be null?
Yes, the version can be set to null. Users can pass null today in the constructor too.
Is there a functional difference between empty and null?
No. Both values indicate the version is not set.
